description: Curated terminology for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and motor neurone disease discovery.

synopsis.overview: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), the most common form of motor neurone disease, is a progressive disorder that damages the nerve cells controlling voluntary muscles.
synopsis.manifestations: It commonly causes increasing weakness, stiffness, cramps or twitching and can later affect movement, speech, swallowing and breathing. Symptoms and their rate of change vary.
synopsis.management: There is no cure. Specialist multidisciplinary care may include medicines that can slow progression for some people, symptom relief, respiratory and nutritional support, physiotherapy, mobility equipment and communication aids.
synopsis.outlook: ALS is usually life-shortening and progresses over months or years, but its course differs substantially between people. The care team can provide information relevant to an individual situation.

topics.heading: Clinical trials
topics.description: Registered ALS and motor neurone disease studies, including recruitment, study progress and reported results. A listing does not indicate eligibility or that a study is recommended.

topics.heading: Treatments
topics.description: Medicines and multidisciplinary ALS care, including symptom management, respiratory and nutritional support, rehabilitation and assistive care.

termDefinitions.riluzole: A medicine used for ALS that reduces glutamate activity and can modestly slow disease progression for some people.
termDefinitions.edaravone: A medicine used for ALS that acts as an antioxidant and may slow functional decline for some people.
termDefinitions.tofersen: An antisense medicine for adults with ALS associated with a harmful SOD1 gene variant; it targets SOD1 messenger RNA.

topics.heading: Research
topics.description: Research into motor-neuron biology, disease progression, biomarkers and new approaches to ALS care and treatment.

termDefinitions.neuron: A nerve cell that receives and transmits information. ALS principally damages motor neurons that control voluntary muscles.
termDefinitions.laboratory: A controlled setting where scientists examine biological samples, cells, models or data before findings may be studied clinically.

topics.heading: Genetics
topics.description: Inherited and genetic contributors to ALS, including genes such as C9orf72 and SOD1 and research into gene-targeted approaches.

termDefinitions.c9orf72: A gene in which an expanded repeated DNA sequence is a common genetic cause of familial ALS and frontotemporal dementia.
termDefinitions.sod1: A gene that makes the superoxide dismutase 1 enzyme. Certain harmful SOD1 variants can cause inherited ALS.
termDefinitions.fus: A gene involved in processing RNA. Certain harmful FUS variants can cause ALS, often through altered FUS protein behavior.
termDefinitions.tardbp: A gene that makes the TDP-43 protein. Harmful variants can cause ALS, and abnormal TDP-43 is found in most ALS cases.

topics.heading: Living with ALS
topics.description: Daily life with ALS, including mobility, communication, nutrition, breathing support, accessibility and quality of life.

topics.heading: Caregiving
topics.description: Practical and emotional information for family, professional and community caregivers, including coordinated, palliative and respite care.

topics.heading: Advocacy
topics.description: ALS awareness, access, public policy, community action and fundraising for care and research.
